source.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה וְאֶֽל־אַהֲרֹ֖ן לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses and to Aaron, saying,

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses and Aaron. He said,
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses and Aaron,

decisions.choice: a remedy for the uncleanness of death, given after many had died
decisions.reason: Chapters 16-17 tell of thousands who died in the rebellion and the plague that followed (Numbers 17:14), and the people cried out that everyone who came near the tabernacle would die (17:27-28). Chapter 18 set the priests and Levites as a guard around the holy place. This chapter gives the way for anyone made unclean by a dead body to be made clean again, so that the camp where the LORD lives is not defiled. The law is spoken to Moses and Aaron together, since it concerns cleanness and the priests' work.

source.text: זֹ֚את חֻקַּ֣ת הַתּוֹרָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר דַּבֵּ֣ר׀אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וְיִקְח֣וּ אֵלֶיךָ֩ פָרָ֨ה אֲדֻמָּ֜ה תְּמִימָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר אֵֽין־בָּהּ֙ מ֔וּם אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹא־עָלָ֥ה עָלֶ֖יהָ עֹֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: This [is the] statute of the law which commanded Yahweh, saying, speak to [the] sons of Israel, and they will take to you [a] heifer red, unblemished, which there [is] not in her [a] blemish, which not has gone up on her [a] yoke.

en.L: "This [is] the statute of the law that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has commanded, saying: Speak to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, that they bring to you a red heifer without defect, in which there is no blemish, on which a yoke has not come.
en.B: "This is the statute of the law that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has commanded: Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} to bring you a red heifer that is perfect, with no defect, and that has never been under a yoke.
en.R: "Here is a rule from the law that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has given. Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} to bring you a red young cow. It must be healthy, with nothing wrong with it. It must never have been put under a yoke to do work.

decisions.choice: the statute of the law: a fixed rule that belongs to the LORD's instruction
decisions.reason: "Statute" is a settled, lasting rule, and "law" here is the LORD's teaching for his people. The two words are joined only here and in 31:21. They mark what follows as a standing ordinance, not a rule for one occasion (verses 10 and 21).

decisions.choice: a red heifer: a young cow, reddish-brown in color
decisions.reason: The word is the female of the bull, a young cow. Red here describes the reddish-brown of cattle. The text does not say why the color was required; it may have called blood to mind, since the blood is burned with the animal (verse 5).

decisions.choice: without defect, never yoked: whole and never put to ordinary work
decisions.reason: An animal for the LORD had to be whole, with no blemish (Leviticus 22:20-22); here the point is stated twice. An animal that had never worn a yoke had never been used for plowing or pulling, so it was kept apart for this purpose (Deuteronomy 21:3; 1 Samuel 6:7).

decisions.choice: speak ... to you: Moses is addressed, and the heifer is brought to him
decisions.reason: "Speak" and "to you" are singular. Moses gives the order to the people, and they bring the animal to him; in verse 3 "you" becomes plural, Moses and Aaron together.

decisions.choice: a red young cow; put under a yoke to do work
decisions.reason: Readable says "young cow" for "heifer", a word many readers do not know, and adds "to do work" to explain what being under a yoke meant.

source.text: וּנְתַתֶּ֣ם אֹתָ֔הּ אֶל־אֶלְעָזָ֖ר הַכֹּהֵ֑ן וְהוֹצִ֤יא אֹתָהּ֙ אֶל־מִח֣וּץ לַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה וְשָׁחַ֥ט אֹתָ֖הּ לְפָנָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will give her to Eleazar the priest, and he will bring her out to outside of the camp, and he will slaughter her before him.

en.L: And you shall give it to Eleazar the priest, and he shall bring it out outside the camp, and [one] shall slaughter it before him.
en.B: You are to give it to Eleazar the priest. It is to be brought outside the camp and slaughtered in his presence.
en.R: Give it to Eleazar the priest. It must be taken outside the camp and killed there while he watches.

decisions.choice: he will bring it out ... slaughter it before him: the person who acts is not named
decisions.reason: The verbs "bring out" and "slaughter" have no named subject. "Before him" shows that Eleazar watches while someone else kills the animal; the one who brings it out may be Eleazar or that other person. The text keeps the focus on Eleazar's oversight.

decisions.choice: Eleazar the priest, not Aaron
decisions.reason: The rite makes those who carry it out unclean (verses 7-10), and the high priest had to keep himself from the uncleanness of the dead (Leviticus 21:11). Eleazar, Aaron's son and successor, already had charge over the Levites and the holy things (3:32; 4:16).

decisions.choice: outside the camp: away from the altar
decisions.reason: Other offerings were killed at the tabernacle. This animal is killed and burned outside the camp, as the remains of the most solemn sin offerings were (Leviticus 4:11-12; 16:27).

decisions.choice: It is to be brought ... and slaughtered
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use passive verbs, which keep the Hebrew's unnamed actor without guessing who it is. Literal keeps "he" and brackets "[one]" for the slaughterer.

source.text: וְלָקַ֞ח אֶלְעָזָ֧ר הַכֹּהֵ֛ן מִדָּמָ֖הּ בְּאֶצְבָּע֑וֹ וְהִזָּ֞ה אֶל־נֹ֨כַח פְּנֵ֧י אֹֽהֶל־מוֹעֵ֛ד מִדָּמָ֖הּ שֶׁ֥בַע פְּעָמִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And will take Eleazar the priest from her blood with his finger, and he will sprinkle toward [the] front of [the] face of [the] tent of meeting from her blood seven times.

en.L: And Eleazar the priest shall take some of its blood with his finger and sprinkle some of its blood toward the front of the tent of meeting seven times.
en.B: Eleazar the priest is to take some of its blood on his finger and sprinkle it seven times toward the front of the tent of meeting.
en.R: Eleazar the priest must put some of its blood on his finger. Then he must sprinkle the blood seven times in the direction of the front of the meeting tent.

decisions.choice: toward the front of the tent of meeting: from outside the camp, facing the sanctuary
decisions.reason: Eleazar stands outside the camp but sprinkles in the direction of the tent's entrance. This ties the rite, done far from the altar, to the LORD's dwelling.

decisions.choice: seven times: a full and complete sprinkling
decisions.reason: Seven is the number of completeness. Blood is sprinkled seven times in other rites of cleansing and atonement (Leviticus 4:6, 17; 14:7; 16:14, 19).

decisions.choice: sprinkle it
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names "some of its blood" twice. Balanced and Readable say it once and refer back to it.

source.text: וְשָׂרַ֥ף אֶת־הַפָּרָ֖ה לְעֵינָ֑יו אֶת־עֹרָ֤הּ וְאֶת־בְּשָׂרָהּ֙ וְאֶת־דָּמָ֔הּ עַל־פִּרְשָׁ֖הּ יִשְׂרֹֽף׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will burn the heifer before his eyes; her skin and her flesh and her blood with her dung he will burn.

en.L: And he shall burn the heifer before his eyes; its skin and its flesh and its blood, with its dung, he shall burn.
en.B: The heifer is to be burned in his sight. Its hide, its flesh and its blood are to be burned along with its dung.
en.R: Then the whole cow must be burned while Eleazar watches. Its skin, its meat, its blood and even its dung must all be burned.

decisions.choice: he will burn ... before his eyes: someone burns it while Eleazar watches
decisions.reason: As in verse 3, the one who acts is not named, and "before his eyes" refers to Eleazar. Verse 8 speaks of "the one who burns it" as a person of his own.

decisions.choice: skin, flesh, blood and dung: the whole animal is burned
decisions.reason: In other offerings the blood was poured out at the altar and the skin went to the priest (Leviticus 7:8). Here everything, blood included, is burned to make the ashes. The remains of the sin offering for the priest and the people were also burned whole outside the camp (Leviticus 4:11-12).

decisions.choice: dung: the contents of the intestines
decisions.reason: The word names the waste inside the animal's gut, which elsewhere is carried out and burned with the rest (Exodus 29:14; Leviticus 16:27).

decisions.choice: the whole cow; even its dung
decisions.reason: Readable adds "whole" and "even" to bring out the point of the list: nothing of the animal is held back. It names Eleazar for "his".

source.text: וְלָקַ֣ח הַכֹּהֵ֗ן עֵ֥ץ אֶ֛רֶז וְאֵז֖וֹב וּשְׁנִ֣י תוֹלָ֑עַת וְהִשְׁלִ֕יךְ אֶל־תּ֖וֹךְ שְׂרֵפַ֥ת הַפָּרָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And will take the priest wood of cedar and hyssop and scarlet of worm, and he will throw [them] into [the] midst of [the] burning of the heifer.

en.L: And the priest shall take cedar wood and hyssop and scarlet yarn, and throw [them] into the midst of the burning of the heifer.
en.B: The priest is to take cedar wood, hyssop and scarlet yarn and throw them into the fire that is burning the heifer.
en.R: The priest must take some cedar wood, a hyssop plant and some red yarn. He must throw them into the fire where the cow is burning.

decisions.choice: cedar wood, hyssop and scarlet yarn: the three things used in cleansing from skin disease
decisions.reason: The same three are used to cleanse a person healed of a skin disease (Leviticus 14:4, 6, 49-52). Cedar is a lasting, fragrant wood; hyssop is a small leafy plant used to sprinkle (verse 18; Exodus 12:22); "scarlet of worm" is wool or thread dyed crimson with a dye made from an insect. Their ashes become part of the heifer's ashes.

decisions.choice: the priest: Eleazar
decisions.reason: No other priest has been named in the rite, so "the priest" here and in verse 7 is Eleazar.

decisions.choice: scarlet yarn / red yarn
decisions.reason: "Scarlet of worm" names the color and the source of the dye; the material was dyed wool or thread. Literal and Balanced say "scarlet yarn" and Readable "red yarn", as in Leviticus 14:4.

source.text: וְכִבֶּ֨ס בְּגָדָ֜יו הַכֹּהֵ֗ן וְרָחַ֤ץ בְּשָׂרוֹ֙ בַּמַּ֔יִם וְאַחַ֖ר יָב֣וֹא אֶל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה וְטָמֵ֥א הַכֹּהֵ֖ן עַד־הָעָֽרֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: And will wash his clothes the priest, and he will bathe his flesh in the water, and after he will come into the camp; and will be unclean the priest until the evening.

en.L: And the priest shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and afterward he may come into the camp; and the priest shall be unclean until the evening.
en.B: Then the priest must wash his clothes and bathe his body in water. After that he may come into the camp, but he will remain unclean until evening.
en.R: After that, the priest must wash his clothes and take a bath. Then he may come back into the camp. But he will still be unclean until evening.

decisions.choice: the priest becomes unclean: the rite that cleanses others makes its workers unclean
decisions.reason: Everyone who takes part in making the ashes, or later sprinkles the water, becomes unclean for the day (verses 8, 10, 21). The text does not say why. The ashes deal with the uncleanness of death, and handling them is treated as contact with that uncleanness.

decisions.choice: until the evening: for the rest of the day
decisions.reason: The day began at evening (Genesis 1:5), so this is the shortest kind of uncleanness, as in Leviticus 11:24-25; it ends with washing and sunset.

decisions.choice: his body
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "his flesh", which here means the whole body. Readable says "take a bath".

source.text: וְהַשֹּׂרֵ֣ף אֹתָ֔הּ יְכַבֵּ֤ס בְּגָדָיו֙ בַּמַּ֔יִם וְרָחַ֥ץ בְּשָׂר֖וֹ בַּמָּ֑יִם וְטָמֵ֖א עַד־הָעָֽרֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: And the [one] burning her will wash his clothes in the water and bathe his flesh in the water, and he will be unclean until the evening.

en.L: And the one who burns it shall wash his clothes in water and bathe his body in water, and he shall be unclean until the evening.
en.B: The one who burns it must also wash his clothes in water and bathe his body in water, and he too will be unclean until evening.
en.R: The one who burned the cow must also wash his clothes and take a bath. He will be unclean until evening too.

decisions.choice: the one who burns it: a helper, not the priest
decisions.reason: This is the person who burned the heifer while Eleazar watched (verse 5). The same washing and the same short uncleanness apply to him as to the priest.

decisions.choice: also; too
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "also" and "too" to show that this verse repeats the rule of verse 7 for a second person.

source.text: וְאָסַ֣ף׀אִ֣ישׁ טָה֗וֹר אֵ֚ת אֵ֣פֶר הַפָּרָ֔ה וְהִנִּ֛יחַ מִח֥וּץ לַֽמַּחֲנֶ֖ה בְּמָק֣וֹם טָה֑וֹר וְ֠הָיְתָה לַעֲדַ֨ת בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֧ל לְמִשְׁמֶ֛רֶת לְמֵ֥י נִדָּ֖ה חַטָּ֥את הִֽוא׃

records.literal_gloss: And will gather a man clean the ashes of the heifer, and he will deposit [them] outside of the camp in a place clean, and it will be for [the] congregation of [the] sons of Israel for keeping, for water of impurity; [a] sin offering it [is].

en.L: And a clean man shall gather up the ashes of the heifer and put [them] outside the camp in a clean place; and it shall be for the congregation of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel for keeping, for water of impurity; it [is] a sin offering.
en.B: A man who is clean is to gather up the ashes of the heifer and put them in a clean place outside the camp. They are to be kept for the congregation of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, for the water to remove impurity. It is a sin offering.
en.R: Then a man who is clean must gather up the cow's ashes. He must put them in a clean place outside the camp. They will be kept there for the community of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. They will use them to make the water that takes away uncleanness. This is a sin offering.

decisions.choice: water of impurity: water for removing impurity
decisions.reason: The noun means impurity. It is used of a woman's monthly uncleanness (Leviticus 15:19) and of what is unclean or abhorrent (Ezra 9:11). The phrase names the water by the uncleanness it deals with: it is the water that takes impurity away, mixed from these ashes (verse 17).

decisions.choice: it is a sin offering: an offering that cleanses
decisions.reason: The word for "sin offering" comes from the verb used for purifying in verses 12, 13, 19 and 20. Though this animal is killed and burned outside the camp and its ashes are kept, it is counted as a sin offering: its purpose is to remove impurity so that the unclean can come back near the LORD.

decisions.choice: for keeping: a supply stored for later use
decisions.reason: The ashes are not used at once but stored in a clean place, so that a little can be mixed with water whenever someone becomes unclean. The ashes of one heifer could serve many times.

decisions.choice: the water to remove impurity / the water that takes away uncleanness
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "water of impurity". Balanced and Readable say what the water is for, since "water of impurity" could be read as water that is itself impure. The same wording is used through the chapter.

source.text: וְ֠כִבֶּס הָאֹסֵ֨ף אֶת־אֵ֤פֶר הַפָּרָה֙ אֶת־בְּגָדָ֔יו וְטָמֵ֖א עַד־הָעָ֑רֶב וְֽהָיְתָ֞ה לִבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וְלַגֵּ֛ר הַגָּ֥ר בְּתוֹכָ֖ם לְחֻקַּ֥ת עוֹלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And will wash the [one] gathering the ashes of the heifer his clothes, and he will be unclean until the evening; and it will be for [the] sons of Israel and for the sojourner who sojourns in their midst as [a] statute forever.

en.L: And the one who gathers the ashes of the heifer shall wash his clothes and be unclean until the evening. And it shall be for the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel and for the sojourner who sojourns among them a statute forever.
en.B: The one who gathers up the ashes of the heifer must wash his clothes, and he will be unclean until evening. This is to be a lasting statute for the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and for the outsider who lives among them.
en.R: The man who gathers up the ashes must wash his clothes, and he will be unclean until evening. This is a law for all time. It is for the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and for strangers who live among them.

decisions.choice: it shall be ... a statute forever: the whole rite as a lasting rule
decisions.reason: "It" refers to the rule of the heifer and its ashes set out in verses 2-10, which is to stand for every generation, as in 15:15. Even the clean man who gathers the ashes becomes unclean, like the priest and the one who burned the heifer.

decisions.choice: the sojourner: a foreigner living among Israel
decisions.reason: The sojourner was someone from another people who had settled among the Israelites. The same means of cleansing is for them as well, as other laws give them the same rule (15:15-16; 9:14).

decisions.choice: the outsider who lives among them / strangers who live among them
decisions.reason: As in 15:15, Literal keeps "sojourner"; Balanced says "outsider" and Readable "strangers".

source.text: הַנֹּגֵ֥עַ בְּמֵ֖ת לְכָל־נֶ֣פֶשׁ אָדָ֑ם וְטָמֵ֖א שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: The [one] touching [the] dead of any corpse of [a] person will be unclean seven days.

en.L: The one who touches the dead [body] of any human person shall be unclean seven days.
en.B: Whoever touches the dead body of any human being will be unclean for seven days.
en.R: Anyone who touches the body of a dead person will be unclean for seven days.

decisions.choice: the dead of any person of a human: a human corpse
decisions.reason: The word usually means a living being, but in laws about uncleanness it can mean a dead person, as in 5:2 and 9:6. Adding "human" makes clear that the rule is about human bodies; dead animals are dealt with in Leviticus 11.

decisions.choice: seven days: the strongest uncleanness from contact
decisions.reason: Touching most unclean things lasted only "until the evening" (verses 7-10; Leviticus 11:24). Contact with a human corpse lasted a full week and needed the water of verse 9 to end it.

decisions.choice: unclean, not guilty
decisions.reason: Becoming unclean by a dead body was not a sin; the dead had to be buried and mourned (Leviticus 21:1-3). But death is the opposite of the living God, and what came from death had to be cleansed before a person could come near his dwelling (verse 13).

source.text: ה֣וּא יִתְחַטָּא־ב֞וֹ בַּיּ֧וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֛י וּבַיּ֥וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֖י יִטְהָ֑ר וְאִם־לֹ֨א יִתְחַטָּ֜א בַּיּ֧וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֛י וּבַיּ֥וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֖י לֹ֥א יִטְהָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: He will purify himself with it on the day the third and on the day the seventh [and] he will be clean; and if not he purifies himself on the day the third and on the day the seventh, not he will be clean.

en.L: He shall purify himself with it on the third day and on the seventh day, and [then] he will be clean; but if he does not purify himself on the third day and on the seventh day, he will not be clean.
en.B: They must purify themselves with the water on the third day and on the seventh day, and then they will be clean. But if they do not purify themselves on the third day and the seventh day, they will not be clean.
en.R: On the third day and on the seventh day they must make themselves clean with the water. Then they will be clean. If they do not do this on both days, they will not be clean.

decisions.choice: with it: with the water for impurity
decisions.reason: "It" points back to the water of verse 9, made from the ashes. Verses 17-19 explain how it is mixed and sprinkled.

decisions.choice: purify himself: rid himself of uncleanness
decisions.reason: The verb is a form of the root behind "sin offering" (verse 9). In this form it means to free oneself from what makes one unclean, here by having the water sprinkled on oneself (verse 19).

decisions.choice: the third day and the seventh day: two sprinklings
decisions.reason: The cleansing takes two stages, the first halfway through the week and the second at its end. Missing either one leaves the person unclean.

decisions.choice: they; the water
decisions.reason: The law covers men and women alike, so Balanced and Readable use "they" for the person. Literal keeps "he" and "himself", as the Hebrew has them. Balanced and Readable also say "the water" for "it".

source.text: כָּֽל־הַנֹּגֵ֡עַ בְּמֵ֣ת בְּנֶפֶשׁ֩ הָאָדָ֨ם אֲשֶׁר־יָמ֜וּת וְלֹ֣א יִתְחַטָּ֗א אֶת־מִשְׁכַּ֤ן יְהוָה֙ טִמֵּ֔א וְנִכְרְתָ֛ה הַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַהִ֖וא מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּי֩ מֵ֨י נִדָּ֜ה לֹא־זֹרַ֤ק עָלָיו֙ טָמֵ֣א יִהְיֶ֔ה ע֖וֹד טֻמְאָת֥וֹ בֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Anyone touching [the] dead, [the] corpse of the person who dies, and not he purifies himself, the tabernacle of Yahweh he has defiled, and will be cut off the person that from Israel; for [the] water of impurity not was sprinkled on him, unclean he will be; still his uncleanness [is] on him.

en.L: Everyone who touches the dead, the body of a person who has died, and does not purify himself, has made the tabernacle of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} unclean; and that person shall be cut off from Israel. Because the water of impurity was not sprinkled on him, he shall be unclean; his uncleanness [is] still on him.
en.B: Anyone who touches a dead body, the body of someone who has died, and does not purify themselves makes the tabernacle of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} unclean, and that person must be cut off from Israel. The water to remove impurity was not sprinkled on them, so they remain unclean; their uncleanness is still on them.
en.R: Suppose someone touches the body of a person who has died and does not make themselves clean. Then they make the tabernacle of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} unclean. That person must be cut off from Israel. The water that takes away uncleanness was not sprinkled on them, so they are still unclean. Their uncleanness has not gone away.

decisions.choice: has made the tabernacle of the LORD unclean
decisions.reason: The LORD lived among his people (5:3), and uncleanness left in the camp was thought of as reaching his dwelling, even without the person going near it (Leviticus 15:31). That is why an uncleansed person was a danger to the whole people.

decisions.choice: cut off from Israel: removed from the people
decisions.reason: As in 15:30, the person loses their place in Israel. The law does not say here whether by the people's action or by God's own judgment.

decisions.choice: because ... still on him: the reason the person stays unclean
decisions.reason: The last part of the verse explains the first: the uncleanness does not wear off with time. Without the water it stays on the person, however long ago the contact was.

decisions.choice: themselves; they; their
decisions.reason: The law covers men and women alike, so Balanced and Readable use "they" for the person. Literal keeps "he" and "himself", as the Hebrew has them.

source.text: זֹ֚את הַתּוֹרָ֔ה אָדָ֖ם כִּֽי־יָמ֣וּת בְּאֹ֑הֶל כָּל־הַבָּ֤א אֶל־הָאֹ֨הֶל֙ וְכָל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּאֹ֔הֶל יִטְמָ֖א שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: This [is] the law: [a] person when he dies in [a] tent, everyone coming into the tent and everyone who [is] in the tent will be unclean seven days.

en.L: This [is] the law when a person dies in a tent: everyone who comes into the tent and everyone who [is] in the tent shall be unclean seven days.
en.B: This is the law when someone dies in a tent: everyone who enters the tent and everyone who is in it will be unclean for seven days.
en.R: This is the law for when someone dies inside a tent. Everyone who goes into the tent will be unclean for seven days. So will everyone who was already inside.

decisions.choice: this is the law: the instruction for a particular case
decisions.reason: "Law" here is a rule for one kind of case, as in "the law of the burnt offering" (Leviticus 6:2). Verses 14-16 add cases to the general rule of verse 11.

decisions.choice: in a tent: uncleanness passes without touch
decisions.reason: A dead body makes unclean everyone under the same roof, whether they touch it or not, and whether they were there at the death or came in later. In the wilderness the tent was the home; the same would hold for a house.

decisions.choice: already inside
decisions.reason: Readable adds "already" to make clear the difference between the two groups: those who come in and those who were there.

source.text: וְכֹל֙ כְּלִ֣י פָת֔וּחַ אֲשֶׁ֛ר אֵין־צָמִ֥יד פָּתִ֖יל עָלָ֑יו טָמֵ֖א הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And every vessel open which there [is] not [a] cover [of] cord on it, unclean it [is].

en.L: And every open vessel that has no cover tied on it [is] unclean.
en.B: Any open container that has no lid tied down on it is unclean.
en.R: Any jar or pot that is left open, without a lid tied on it, will be unclean.

decisions.choice: a cover of cord: a lid fastened down with a cord
decisions.reason: The first word means something bound or fastened; the second is a cord or thread. Together they describe a lid tied tight so that the vessel is closed.

decisions.choice: every open vessel is unclean: what is sealed is protected
decisions.reason: A vessel standing open in the tent shares the uncleanness of the place, with whatever is in it. One closed with a tied lid does not. Compare Leviticus 11:33, where a clay pot an unclean thing falls into becomes unclean.

decisions.choice: container; jar or pot
decisions.reason: The word covers any household article; here it is something that can be open or closed, so Balanced says "container" and Readable names common examples.

source.text: וְכֹ֨ל אֲשֶׁר־יִגַּ֜ע עַל־פְּנֵ֣י הַשָּׂדֶ֗ה בַּֽחֲלַל־חֶ֨רֶב֙ א֣וֹ בְמֵ֔ת אֽוֹ־בְעֶ֥צֶם אָדָ֖ם א֣וֹ בְקָ֑בֶר יִטְמָ֖א שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And everyone who touches on [the] face of the field [one] slain [by the] sword or [a] dead [person] or [a] bone of [a] human or [a] grave will be unclean seven days.

en.L: And everyone who, on the face of the field, touches one slain by the sword, or a dead [person], or a human bone, or a grave, shall be unclean seven days.
en.B: Anyone out in the open field who touches someone killed by the sword, or someone who has died, or a human bone, or a grave, will be unclean for seven days.
en.R: Someone out in the open country may touch a person who was killed with a sword or who died in some other way. Or they may touch a human bone or a grave. Anyone who does this will be unclean for seven days.

decisions.choice: on the face of the field: out in the open, away from any tent
decisions.reason: Verse 14 dealt with a death under a roof. This verse covers a body or remains found in open country, where only touching makes a person unclean.

decisions.choice: one slain by the sword or a dead person: killed by violence or dead of any other cause
decisions.reason: The first word is used of those killed in battle or by violence; the second of anyone who has died. The law covers both.

decisions.choice: a human bone or a grave: remains and burial places also make unclean
decisions.reason: Uncleanness comes not only from a recent body but from bones and from graves. Touching a tomb made a person unclean for the full seven days.

decisions.choice: who died in some other way
decisions.reason: Readable adds "in some other way" to show that "a dead person" is set against one killed by the sword.

source.text: וְלָֽקְחוּ֙ לַטָּמֵ֔א מֵעֲפַ֖ר שְׂרֵפַ֣ת הַֽחַטָּ֑את וְנָתַ֥ן עָלָ֛יו מַ֥יִם חַיִּ֖ים אֶל־כֶּֽלִי׃

records.literal_gloss: And they will take for the unclean [one] from [the] dust of [the] burning of the sin offering, and he will put on it living water into [a] vessel.

en.L: And for the unclean [person] they shall take some of the dust of the burning of the sin offering, and [one] shall put living water on it in a vessel.
en.B: For the unclean person, some of the ashes of the burned sin offering are to be taken and put in a container, and fresh water is to be poured on them.
en.R: To make the unclean person clean, someone must take some ashes from the burned sin offering and put them in a jar. Then fresh running water must be poured on them.

decisions.choice: they will take ... he will put: the persons who act are not named
decisions.reason: The verbs have no stated subject. Anyone clean may do it; verse 18 names "a clean man" for the sprinkling.

decisions.choice: the dust of the burning of the sin offering: the stored ashes
decisions.reason: "Dust" here means the fine ash left from burning the heifer, which verse 9 calls ashes and a sin offering.

decisions.choice: living water: water from a spring or stream
decisions.reason: "Living" water is fresh, running water, not water standing in a cistern (Genesis 26:19; Leviticus 14:5).

decisions.choice: are to be taken ... fresh water is to be poured
decisions.reason: Balanced uses passive verbs to keep the unnamed actors, and Readable says "someone". Both say "fresh water" for "living water"; Readable adds "running" and "To make the unclean person clean" to say what the mixture is for.

source.text: וְלָקַ֨ח אֵז֜וֹב וְטָבַ֣ל בַּמַּיִם֮ אִ֣ישׁ טָהוֹר֒ וְהִזָּ֤ה עַל־הָאֹ֨הֶל֙ וְעַל־כָּל־הַכֵּלִ֔ים וְעַל־הַנְּפָשׁ֖וֹת אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָֽיוּ־שָׁ֑ם וְעַל־הַנֹּגֵ֗עַ בַּעֶ֨צֶם֙ א֣וֹ בֶֽחָלָ֔ל א֥וֹ בַמֵּ֖ת א֥וֹ בַקָּֽבֶר׃

records.literal_gloss: And will take hyssop and dip in the water a man clean, and he will sprinkle on the tent and on all the vessels and on the persons who were there, and on the [one] touching the bone or the slain or the dead or the grave.

en.L: And a clean man shall take hyssop and dip [it] in the water and sprinkle [it] on the tent and on all the vessels and on the persons who were there, and on the one who touched the bone, or the slain, or the dead, or the grave.
en.B: Then a man who is clean is to take hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle the tent, all its furnishings and the people who were there. He is also to sprinkle anyone who touched a bone, or someone killed, or someone who died, or a grave.
en.R: Then a man who is clean must take a hyssop branch and dip it in the water. He must sprinkle the water on the tent, on everything in it and on the people who were there. He must also sprinkle anyone who touched a bone, a person who was killed or died, or a grave.

decisions.choice: hyssop: a small plant used as a sprinkler
decisions.reason: Hyssop has leafy stems that hold liquid, and a bunch of it was used to sprinkle or smear (Exodus 12:22; Leviticus 14:6). The hyssop burned with the heifer (verse 6) is matched by hyssop used to sprinkle its water.

decisions.choice: a clean man: any clean person, not only a priest
decisions.reason: The sprinkler is not said to be a priest. Any man who is clean may do it, so that the rite can be carried out wherever someone has died.

decisions.choice: the vessels and the persons: everything and everyone made unclean by the death
decisions.reason: "Vessels" covers all the articles in the tent, including the open containers of verse 15. "Persons" are the people who were in the tent (verse 14), and the rest of the verse adds those made unclean in the open (verse 16).

decisions.choice: furnishings
decisions.reason: Balanced says "furnishings" for the articles of a tent. Literal keeps "vessels" and Readable "everything in it".

source.text: וְהִזָּ֤ה הַטָּהֹר֙ עַל־הַטָּמֵ֔א בַּיּ֥וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֖י וּבַיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֑י וְחִטְּאוֹ֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י וְכִבֶּ֧ס בְּגָדָ֛יו וְרָחַ֥ץ בַּמַּ֖יִם וְטָהֵ֥ר בָּעָֽרֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: And will sprinkle the clean [one] on the unclean [one] on the day the third and on the day the seventh, and he will purify him on the day the seventh; and he will wash his clothes and bathe in the water, and he will be clean in the evening.

en.L: And the clean [man] shall sprinkle [it] on the unclean [person] on the third day and on the seventh day, and he shall purify him on the seventh day; and he shall wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be clean at evening.
en.B: The clean man is to sprinkle the unclean person on the third day and on the seventh day, and on the seventh day he will have purified them. Then the one being cleansed must wash their clothes and bathe in water, and at evening they will be clean.
en.R: The clean man must sprinkle the unclean person on the third day and on the seventh day. On the seventh day he will finish making them clean. Then they must wash their clothes and take a bath. At evening they will be clean.

decisions.choice: he will purify him ... he will wash: the subject changes
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses "he" throughout. The clean man is the one who sprinkles and so purifies the unclean person; the one who washes his clothes, bathes and becomes clean is the person being cleansed, as in verse 12.

decisions.choice: purify: remove uncleanness
decisions.reason: This verb is the active form of the one in verse 12: the clean man frees the other from uncleanness by the sprinkling.

decisions.choice: clean at evening: the last step, as in other cleansings
decisions.reason: The seventh-day sprinkling is followed by washing and bathing, and the person is clean when the new day begins at evening (Leviticus 14:9; 15:13).

decisions.choice: the clean man; the one being cleansed; they
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who does each thing, where the Hebrew uses "he" for both men. The law covers men and women alike, so Balanced and Readable use "they" for the person. Literal keeps "he" and "himself", as the Hebrew has them.

source.text: וְאִ֤ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־יִטְמָא֙ וְלֹ֣א יִתְחַטָּ֔א וְנִכְרְתָ֛ה הַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַהִ֖וא מִתּ֣וֹךְ הַקָּהָ֑ל כִּי֩ אֶת־מִקְדַּ֨שׁ יְהוָ֜ה טִמֵּ֗א מֵ֥י נִדָּ֛ה לֹא־זֹרַ֥ק עָלָ֖יו טָמֵ֥א הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And [a] man who is unclean and not he purifies himself, and will be cut off the person that from [the] midst of the assembly, for the sanctuary of Yahweh he has defiled; [the] water of impurity not has been sprinkled on him; unclean he [is].

en.L: But {{gender:a person|a man}} who is unclean and does not purify himself, that person shall be cut off from the midst of the assembly, for he has made the sanctuary of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} unclean; the water of impurity has not been sprinkled on him; he [is] unclean.
en.B: But anyone who is unclean and does not purify themselves must be cut off from among the assembly, because they have made the sanctuary of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} unclean. The water to remove impurity has not been sprinkled on them; they are unclean.
en.R: But suppose someone who is unclean does not make themselves clean. That person must be cut off from the assembly, because they have made the holy place of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} unclean. The water that takes away uncleanness was not sprinkled on them, so they are unclean.

decisions.choice: a man: anyone, man or woman
decisions.reason: The word is "man", but as in Leviticus 27:2 it means any person; the verse goes on to say "that person".

decisions.choice: a second warning, matching verse 13
decisions.reason: The warning of verse 13 is repeated, with "the assembly" for "Israel" and "the sanctuary" for "the tabernacle". Saying it twice stresses how serious it is to neglect the cleansing.

decisions.choice: the sanctuary: the holy place where the LORD lives
decisions.reason: The word means a holy place. It names the same dwelling as "the tabernacle" in verse 13, seen as set apart for the LORD.

decisions.choice: a person / anyone; themselves; they
decisions.reason: Literal uses the gender setting for "man" and keeps "he" after it. The law covers men and women alike, so Balanced and Readable use "they" for the person. Literal keeps "he" and "himself", as the Hebrew has them.

source.text: וְהָיְתָ֥ה לָּהֶ֖םלְחֻקַּ֣ת עוֹלָ֑ם וּמַזֵּ֤ה מֵֽי־הַנִּדָּה֙ יְכַבֵּ֣ס בְּגָדָ֔יו וְהַנֹּגֵ֨עַ֙ בְּמֵ֣י הַנִּדָּ֔ה יִטְמָ֖א עַד־הָעָֽרֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be for them as [a] statute forever; and [the one] sprinkling [the] water of the impurity will wash his clothes, and the [one] touching [the] water of the impurity will be unclean until the evening.

en.L: And it shall be a statute forever for them. And the one who sprinkles the water of impurity shall wash his clothes, and the one who touches the water of impurity shall be unclean until the evening.
en.B: This is to be a lasting statute for them. The one who sprinkles the water to remove impurity must wash his clothes, and anyone who touches that water will be unclean until evening.
en.R: This is a law for them for all time. The man who sprinkles the water that takes away uncleanness must wash his clothes. And anyone who touches that water will be unclean until evening.

decisions.choice: the water that cleanses the unclean makes the clean unclean
decisions.reason: As with the priest and the helpers in verses 7-10, the water that ends the uncleanness of death makes those who handle it unclean for the day. The text states it without explaining it.

decisions.choice: for them: for the Israelites
decisions.reason: "Them" are the Israelites and the outsiders living among them, named in verse 10, where the same phrase is used.

decisions.choice: that water
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "that water" the second time instead of repeating the full name.

source.text: וְכֹ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־יִגַּע־בּ֥וֹ הַטָּמֵ֖א יִטְמָ֑א וְהַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַנֹּגַ֖עַת תִּטְמָ֥א עַד־הָעָֽרֶב׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And all that touches in it the unclean [one] will be unclean, and the person touching will be unclean until the evening.

en.L: And anything that the unclean [person] touches shall be unclean, and the person who touches [it] shall be unclean until the evening."
en.B: Anything the unclean person touches becomes unclean, and anyone who touches it will be unclean until evening."
en.R: Anything an unclean person touches becomes unclean. Anyone who touches it will be unclean until evening."

decisions.choice: the person who touches: touches what the unclean person touched
alternatives: the person who touches the unclean person
decisions.reason: The verb has no object. It most likely means the thing the unclean person has touched. It could also mean the unclean person himself; either way the uncleanness passed on in this way lasts only until evening.

decisions.choice: uncleanness passed on grows weaker
decisions.reason: The dead make a person unclean for seven days; what that person touches becomes unclean too, and contact with it lasts only until evening, as with other uncleanness in Leviticus 15:5-11.

decisions.choice: [it]; it
decisions.reason: English needs an object for "touches". "It" refers to the thing just mentioned; the speech that began in verse 2 closes here.
